newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade $69, light - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade $69, light - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales were light at $69.00 per cwt, unchanged from Tuesday's hefty sales, feedlot sources said.
About 200 steers sold in the Texas Panhandle, which brought the week to date volume near 79,000, they said.
An estimated 600 head sold in Kansas, which elevated the weekly movement to 82,300, the sources said.

Fed cattle prices were supported by strong beef demand and smaller supplies of market-ready cattle on this week's showlists, they said. Finished cattle supplies were thinned by heavy sales last week, feedlot sources said.
Beef prices, however, were seen near a top as more retailers complete booking orders for Memorial Day holiday features, market sources said.
Beef prices Wednesday were quoted down $0.74 to $1.10 per cwt, with 280 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.

Cattle slaughter was estimated at 131,000 head on Wednesday, compared with 133,000 last week and 131,000 last year, USDA said. The week to date number was pegged at 402,000, up 2.8 percent from a week ago and up 2.3 percent from a year ago, USDA statistics showed.
